# Purpose and scope

This Process Characterization Plan (**PCP-009**) defines the Stage 1 (Process Design)
characterization of the A-Mab small-virus retentive filtration step (Step 9), the dedicated
size-based virus-removal operation that follows the anion-exchange polish and precedes final
ultrafiltration / diafiltration. Virus filtration removes small non-enveloped virus by a
**mechanistic, size-exclusion mechanism that is orthogonal** to the low-pH inactivation
(Step 6) and the charge-based anion-exchange clearance (Step 8); it is the **principal
contributor to the cumulative MVM (parvovirus) log-reduction** and a major contributor to
the enveloped-virus (XMuLV) log-reduction. The plan specifies the objectives, the attributes
in scope, the process parameters and ranges to be characterized, the experimental designs,
the analytical (virus-spiking) methods, the sampling plan, the statistical-analysis
approach, and the acceptance and decision criteria by which each parameter will be classified
and the volumetric-load limit established.

**Scope.** The commercial-scale small-virus retentive filtration step, characterized on a
qualified scale-down filtration model with validated live-virus spiking studies. The upstream
anion-exchange step (Step 8), which defines the feed to this step, and the downstream UF/DF
step (Step 10) are addressed only where they define the feed to, or the feed from, this
operation; their characterization is out of scope. This plan governs execution only — the
results are reported in the paired Process Characterization Report (**PCR-009**).

**Basis.** The unit-operation model, quality-attribute framework and risk methodology follow
the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]; viral clearance is evaluated and credited per ICH Q5A(R2)
[@ichq5a], including orthogonal (modular) clearance and worst-case substantiation; the Stage 1
approach and report structure follow PDA TR 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good Practice Guide
[@ispegpg2023]; the QbD framework follows ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11] and
the lifecycle approach of the FDA 2011 guidance [@fda2011].

# Objectives

The characterization will:

1. establish the quantitative relationship between the filtration parameters (volumetric
   load and pressure) and the MVM and XMuLV log-reduction and the step yield;
2. identify the significant main effects, interaction and curvature, including the
   anticipated decline of the MVM log-reduction with volumetric load;
3. establish the volumetric-load limit over which the credited small-virus log-reduction is
   preserved, and substantiate the credited clearance at the worst-case (maximum-load)
   condition per ICH Q5A(R2);
4. establish proven acceptable ranges (PARs) and confirm normal operating ranges (NORs) for
   each parameter;
5. classify each parameter for its risk of impact to the credited viral clearance and to
   process performance (CPP / WC-CPP / KPP / GPP); and
6. provide the process understanding and ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating conditions
   and the drug-substance viral-safety control strategy.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

Small-virus retentive filtration is the dedicated virus-removal step of the A-Mab
purification train: the anion-exchange flow-through pool is passed through a small-virus
retentive (nanometre-rated) filter under controlled pressure, so that virus particles larger
than the membrane rating are retained by size exclusion while the antibody monomer transmits
[@amab2009]. Unlike the upstream operations it forms no new product-quality CQA; its role in
the control strategy is to provide **robust, size-based removal of small non-enveloped virus
(MVM)** together with substantial removal of larger enveloped virus (XMuLV), as an orthogonal
contribution to viral safety. Platform knowledge established that removal is governed by size
exclusion at the membrane rating: the larger enveloped XMuLV is retained essentially
completely and robustly, whereas the small parvovirus MVM — whose size is closer to the
membrane rating — is retained with a log-reduction that is high but declines as the membrane
is progressively loaded, so the credited MVM clearance is a function of the volumetric load;
and that filtration pressure, within a controlled range, does not materially change retention
but must be controlled to preserve filter performance and integrity. This knowledge frames
the attributes in scope and the prioritization of parameters for characterization.

## Quality attributes in scope

Virus filtration introduces no CQA. It is a principal clearance step for the two model
viruses whose cumulative, cross-step log-reduction is specified at the drug substance
(@tbl-cqa): the enveloped retrovirus XMuLV and the small non-enveloped parvovirus MVM.
Criticality is scored on the A-Mab continuum using Tool #1 (Risk Score = Impact ×
Uncertainty); both viral-clearance attributes are rated Very High (VH) and treated as
*Critical* [@amab2009; @ichq5a].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(VF_CQAS))
```

: Viral-clearance CQAs to which the virus-filtration step contributes (expressed as the cumulative, cross-step log-reduction), with acceptance criterion and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty). {#tbl-cqa}

The per-step MVM and XMuLV log-reductions are not themselves released specifications; they
are the modular contributions whose sum, across the low-pH inactivation, anion-exchange and
virus-filtration steps, must meet the cumulative log-reduction requirements at the drug
substance. Because virus filtration is the principal MVM-removal mechanism, the study is
designed to demonstrate the MVM-clearance capacity of the step at and beyond the maximum
routine load; the MVM log-reduction is the primary response of the study.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments and the risk flow of
PDA TR 60, the study scope is set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment
(**RA-001**). A risk-ranking-and-filtering (RRF) screen scores each parameter for its
potential impact and assigns the study type accordingly: the volumetric load and the
filtration pressure — which carry a credible risk to the credited viral log-reduction or must
be controlled to preserve filter performance — are both studied in the multivariate DoE; no
parameter at this step is assigned to univariate assessment [@amab2009]. The resulting
parameter set and study-type assignment are given in @tbl-param.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Characterization will be performed on a scale-down virus-filtration model operated at the
commercial-process equivalents for membrane type and rating, area-normalized load, filtration
pressure, buffer matrix and product concentration (**SOP-2012**). Prior to characterization
the SDM will be qualified against at-scale reference data (**SOP-1001**) by comparing the
operational parameters and, critically, the input and output attributes — volumetric
throughput, MVM and XMuLV log-reduction and step yield — to confirm the model is
representative and suitable to support the load limit and PAR claims [@pdatr60; @ichq5a].
Viral log-reduction will be determined by validated live-virus spiking studies on the
qualified SDM. The centre-point replicates of each design provide an in-study estimate of
model reproducibility (pure error) used in the lack-of-fit assessment.

## Operation

The anion-exchange flow-through pool is filtered through a small-virus retentive membrane of
the platform type and rating under controlled filtration pressure, to a defined
area-normalized volumetric load, with the filtrate collected as the virus-filtration pool.
Product transmits through the membrane while virus larger than the membrane rating is
retained by size exclusion. Membrane lot, pre-use flush and buffer matrix are controlled to
platform specifications and treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than
characterized variables [@amab2009]. A post-use filter-integrity test (**SOP-2012**) confirms
membrane integrity after each run and is a release-linked control for the credited retention.

## Analytical methods

The step responses will be measured by the validated methods in @tbl-methods; method
performance characteristics are per the cited validation reports. The MVM and XMuLV
log-reduction are derived from the infectious titre of the filter load and filtrate in
validated live-virus spiking studies.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=VIRUS_FILT_AMV_REFS))
```

: Validated analytical methods for the characterization. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each DoE run will be sampled at the filter load and the virus-filtration pool for the MVM and
XMuLV infectious titre (spiking studies) and for the step-yield determination; in-process
readings (pressure, flux/throughput and the post-use integrity result) will confirm the
filtration profile and membrane integrity. Centre-point runs are replicated within each
design (three in screening, four in the response-surface design) to quantify reproducibility
and pure error.

## Statistical methods

Designs will be constructed and analyzed in coded factors, with each parameter's
characterization range mapped so that the set-point is 0 and the range edges are
±1 (**SOP-1002**). Screening data will be analyzed by ordinary-least-squares regression of
each response on the main effects and the two-factor interaction; factor effects are reported
as twice the coded coefficient. Response-surface data will be analyzed with the full quadratic
model. Significance will be assessed at α = 0.05. Model adequacy will be judged by R²,
adjusted R², predicted R² (from the PRESS statistic), the overall model F-test, and an ANOVA
lack-of-fit test against the centre-point pure error; a response with no significant parameter
effect will be reported as robust rather than modelled predictively. The volumetric-load limit
will be established from the MVM response and the credited clearance substantiated
conservatively at the worst-case (maximum-load) condition per ICH Q5A(R2). Commercial-scale
capability of the cumulative viral-clearance CQAs to which the step contributes will be
estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation with each parameter varied within its NOR.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

Two parameters are in scope (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each factor ("Range
studied") defines the edges of the explored knowledge space and the basis of the PAR; the NOR
is the tighter routine-control range. Classification is an output of the study and is reported
in PCR-009. The DoE factor coding is given in @tbl-legend.

## Screening design

Factor screening will use a two-level full factorial in the two factors (A = volumetric load,
B = filtration pressure) with three centre-point replicates, `{python} n_scr` runs in total.
The full factorial estimates both main effects and the two-factor interaction without
confounding. Three responses will be recorded for each run (MVM log-reduction, XMuLV
log-reduction and step yield). The planned coded design is given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The two factors will be carried into a face-centred central-composite design with four
centre-point replicates, `{python} n_rsm` runs in total, enabling estimation of curvature in
addition to the main effects and interaction. The planned coded design is given in Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

No parameter at this step is assigned to univariate assessment: both the volumetric load and
the filtration pressure are carried into the multivariate design, the load because it governs
the credited MVM clearance and the pressure so that its (expected small) effect on retention
is quantified jointly with the load rather than assumed.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The study is acceptable when:

1. the SDM qualification confirms representativeness of commercial scale (**SOP-1001**) and
   the spiking studies meet their validity criteria (ICH Q5A(R2));
2. the fitted response-surface model for the MVM log-reduction is adequate — no significant
   lack of fit (p > 0.05 against the centre-point pure error) and residual diagnostics
   without systematic structure — and resolves the volumetric-load dependence (a response
   with no significant factor effect is reported as robust); and
3. a volumetric-load limit exists at or below which the credited MVM log-reduction is
   preserved with margin at the worst-case condition, with the XMuLV log-reduction and step
   yield robust across the NORs.

Each parameter will then be classified per the A-Mab continuum [@amab2009]:

- a parameter whose variability significantly impacts the credited viral clearance is a
  **CPP**; where the impact is reliably controlled within the operating region the parameter
  is a **well-controlled CPP (WC-CPP)**;
- a parameter that does not significantly impact the credited clearance but affects process
  performance or is controlled to protect it is a **KPP** or **WC-CPP** as appropriate;
  otherwise it is a **GPP**.

The load limit, classifications and PARs established here will justify the Stage 2 operating
ranges and feed the drug-substance viral-safety control strategy.

# Data management and integrity

All raw data, DoE designs, spiking-study results and statistical analyses will be recorded and
retained under the site data-integrity procedures (ALCOA+). Analyses will be performed with
version-controlled scripts and reviewed by a second analyst; designs, models and the derived
load limit will be archived with the report. Any deviation from this plan will be documented
and assessed for impact in PCR-009.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable of this plan is the Process Characterization Report (**PCR-009**), reporting
the executed designs, the significant effects, the volumetric-load limit, the parameter
classification and the viral-clearance outcomes. PCR-009 rolls up into the Process
Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter risk basis for the
post-characterization process risk assessment. Execution follows SDM qualification and
precedes the Stage 2 PPQ campaign.

# Risks and assumptions

The plan assumes the SDM is representative of commercial scale (confirmed by qualification)
and that the spiking assays are validated and in control. The principal risk is that the
absolute log-reduction or throughput shifts at commercial scale or across membrane lots, or
that the load presented to the filter is higher than characterized; this is mitigated by
defining the load limit on the qualified SDM, substantiating the credited clearance at the
worst-case load, confirming the limit at scale in Stage 2, and carrying the WC-CPP ranges
forward with the load limit, pressure control and the post-use filter-integrity test.
